title: Tutorial: Work With a List
scenario: A list keeps values in order. Terraform can index a list, count it, or iterate over it. Build a small list of environment names and read the first item and the length.
constraints: Define local.environments as a list of three names.
The first value must be dev and the last must be prod.

focus.title: Create the ordered list
focus.todo: Add three environment names in deployment order.

hints.why: Lists are the starting point for repetition in Terraform. Indexing teaches that positions matter; length teaches how a configuration can adapt when the list grows.
hints.what: Add one local named environments. It should contain three strings in order, starting with dev and ending with prod. The two outputs are already wired to demonstrate indexing and length.
hints.when: Use a list when values have a natural order or when every item is interchangeable. If each item needs a stable name, a map is usually a better fit.
hints.how: Inside `locals`, add `environments = [...]` with three quoted strings in deployment order. The existing outputs already use `local.environments[0]` and `length(local.environments)`, so keep the local name exactly `environments`.

test_manifest.title: the environments list contains the requested names
